claim: HIV and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections are known for impaired neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses.
source: HIV and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections are known for impaired neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by the manuscript's introduction and references to prior literature.

claim: Sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction.
source: While sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction, driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
evidence: This statement is presented as an established understanding in the field, though the manuscript notes that specific molecular drivers remain unknown.

claim: Driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
source: While sequential virus–host B cell interaction appears to be basally required for NAb induction, driver molecular signatures predisposing to NAb induction still remain largely unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals.
source: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals, with seven selecting for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental findings from the screening study.

claim: Seven of the nine NAb-inducing animals selected for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
source: Screening of seventy difficult-to-neutralize SIVmac239-infected macaques found nine NAb-inducing animals, with seven selecting for a specific CD8+ T-cell escape mutation in viral nef before NAb induction.
evidence: This is a key finding from the data analysis showing temporal relationship between mutation selection and NAb induction.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation reduced excess Nef interaction-mediated drive of B-cell maturation-limiting PI3K/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2).
source: This Nef-G63E mutation reduced excess Nef interaction-mediated drive of B-cell maturation-limiting PI3K/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2).
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental assays including proximity ligation assay and co-immunoprecipitation analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells.
source: In vivo imaging cytometry depicted preferential Nef perturbation of cognate Envelope-specific B cells, suggestive of polarized contact-dependent Nef transfer and corroborating cognate B-cell maturation post-mutant selection up to NAb induction.
evidence: This is supported by the imaging flow cytometry data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Results collectively exemplify a NAb induction pattern extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease.
source: Results collectively exemplify a NAb induction pattern extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease and indicate that harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion drawn from the collective experimental findings and comparison with APDS disease.

claim: Harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
source: Results collectively exemplify a NAb induction pattern extrinsically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function antibody-dysregulating disease and indicate that harnessing the PI3K/mTORC2 axis may facilitate NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells.
source: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells (Kumar et al., 2010; Shulman et al., 2014; Gitlin et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014) and often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: NAb responses often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections.
source: Virus-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses by B cells are induced by an intricate cooperation of adaptive immune cells (Kumar et al., 2010; Shulman et al., 2014; Gitlin et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014) and often play a central role in clearance of acute viral infections (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Junt et al., 2007.

claim: Persistence-prone viruses such as HIV-1, SIV, and LCMV variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures.
source: In contrast, persistence-prone viruses such as human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV), and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures (Moir et al., 2001; Mattapallil et al., 2005; Sommerstein et al., 2015; Sammicheli et al., 2016; Fallet et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2016), impairing NAb induction (Levesque et al., 2009; Mikell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Persistence-prone viruses impair NAb induction.
source: In contrast, persistence-prone viruses such as human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV), and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) variously equip themselves with B cell/antibody-inhibitory countermeasures (Moir et al., 2001; Mattapallil et al., 2005; Sommerstein et al., 2015; Sammicheli et al., 2016; Fallet et al., 2016; Mason et al., 2016), impairing NAb induction (Levesque et al., 2009; Mikell et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Levesque et al., 2009 and Mikell et al., 2011.

claim: HIV and SIV successfully suppress elicitation of potent NAb responses, especially in acute infection.
source: These viruses successfully suppress elicitation of potent NAb responses, especially in acute infection (Hunziker et al., 2003; Tomaras et al., 2008), and establish viral persistence, posing considerable challenges for developing protective strategies.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hunziker et al., 2003 and Tomaras et al., 2008.

claim: HIV and SIV establish early a large body of infection in vivo with a distinct host genome-integrating retroviral life cycle.
source: In particular, HIV and SIV establish early a large body of infection in vivo from early on with a distinct host genome-integrating retroviral life cycle (Whitney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Whitney et al., 2014.

claim: HIV and SIV are unique in launching a matrix of host immune-perturbing interactions mainly by their six remarkably pleiotropic accessory viral proteins.
source: In addition, these lentiviruses are unique in launching a matrix of host immune-perturbing interactions mainly by their six remarkably pleiotropic accessory viral proteins, which optimally fuels viral pathogenesis (Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Sheehy et al., 2002; Harris et al., 2003; Schindler et al., 2006; Neil et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2009; Laguette et al., 2011; Yamada et al., 2018; Joas et al., 2018; Langer et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2019; Joas et al., 2020; Khan et al., 2020; Volcic et al., 2020; Reuschl et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by extensive citations to prior literature.

claim: Adverse virus–host interactions in HIV/SIV infection lead to a detrimental consequence of the absence of acute-phase endogenous NAb responses.
source: Adverse virus–host interactions in HIV/SIV infection lead to a detrimental consequence of the absence of acute-phase endogenous NAb responses.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the preceding discussion and established knowledge.

claim: Passive NAb infusion in the acute phase can trigger an endogenous T-cell synergism, resulting in robust control of SIV and chimeric SHIV.
source: Contrasting this, we and others have previously described in in vivo experimental models that passive NAb infusion in the acute phase can trigger an endogenous T-cell synergism, resulting in robust control of SIV and chimeric SHIV (simian/human immunodeficiency virus) (Haigwood et al., 1996; Yamamoto et al., 2007; Ng et al., 2010; Iseda et al., 2016; Nishimura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations including the authors' own prior work.

claim: Virus-specific NAbs not only confer sterile protection but also can evoke T-cell-mediated non-sterile viral control.
source: This indicates that virus-specific NAbs not only confer sterile protection but also can evoke T-cell-mediated non-sterile viral control, suggesting the importance of endogenous NAb responses supported by humoral-cellular response synergisms, during an optimal time frame.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on passive NAb infusion.

claim: Various in vivo signatures of HIV-specific NAb induction, such as antibody-NAb coevolution, autoimmune-driven induction, and natural killer cell-related host polymorphisms, have been reported.
source: Various in vivo signatures of HIV-specific NAb induction, such as antibody-NAb coevolution (Moore et al., 2012), autoimmune-driven induction (Moody et al., 2016), and natural killer cell-related host polymorphisms (Bradley et al., 2018), have been reported to date.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Moore et al., 2012; Moody et al., 2016; and Bradley et al., 2018.

claim: Pathways to NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV are redundant.
source: The broad range of contributing factors collectively, and interestingly, indicates that pathways to NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses including HIV/SIV are redundant, and may potentially involve as-yet-unknown mechanisms driving NAb induction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the diversity of reported mechanisms.

claim: SIVmac239 is pathogenic in rhesus macaques causing simian AIDS across a broad range of geographical origin of macaques.
source: This virus is pathogenic in rhesus macaques causing simian AIDS across a broad range of geographical origin of macaques (Cumont et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cumont et al., 2008.

claim: Macaques infected with SIVmac239 show persistent viremia and generally lack NAb responses throughout infection.
source: Macaques infected with SIVmac239 show persistent viremia and generally lack NAb responses throughout infection (Kestler et al., 1991; Nomura et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kestler et al., 1991 and Nomura et al., 2012.

claim: A large-scale screening of SIVmac239-infected Burmese rhesus macaques for up to 100 weeks identified a subgroup inducing NAbs in the chronic phase.
source: In this study, a large-scale screening of SIVmac239-infected Burmese rhesus macaques for up to 100 weeks identified a subgroup inducing NAbs in the chronic phase.
evidence: This is a direct report of the study's experimental design and findings.

claim: Before NAb induction, NAb-inducing animals commonly selected for a specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) escape mutation in the viral Nef-coding gene.
source: Interestingly, before NAb induction, these animals commonly selected for a specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) escape mutation in the viral Nef-coding gene.
evidence: This is a key finding from the temporal analysis of viral sequences and NAb titers.

claim: The mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2).
source: Compared with wild-type (WT) Nef, this mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), resulting in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt (Omori et al., 2006; Limon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from proximity ligation assay and co-immunoprecipitation shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mutant Nef resulted in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt.
source: Compared with wild-type (WT) Nef, this mutant Nef manifested a decrease in aberrant interaction with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2), resulting in decreased downstream hyperactivation of the canonical B-cell negative regulator Akt (Omori et al., 2006; Limon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing decreased pAkt Ser473 levels in Figure 4B.

claim: Machine learning-assisted imaging cytometry revealed that Nef preferentially targets Env-specific B cells in vivo.
source: Machine learning-assisted imaging cytometry revealed that Nef preferentially targets Env-specific B cells in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the imaging flow cytometry data presented in Figure 5D.

claim: The NAb induction was linked with sustained Env-specific B-cell responses after or during the mutant Nef selection.
source: Furthermore, the NAb induction was linked with sustained Env-specific B-cell responses after or during the mutant Nef selection.
evidence: This is supported by the B-cell response data presented in Figure 7.

claim: NAb induction in SIVmac239-infected hosts conceivably involves a functional boosting of B cells that is phenotypically reciprocal to human PI3K gain-of-function and antibody-dysregulating inborn error of immunity, activated PI3 kinase delta syndrome (APDS).
source: Thus, NAb induction in SIVmac239-infected hosts conceivably involves a functional boosting of B cells that is phenotypically reciprocal to a recently found human PI3K gain-of-function and antibody-dysregulating inborn error of immunity (IEI), activated PI3 kinase delta syndrome (APDS) (Angulo et al., 2013; Lucas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion based on the collective findings and comparison with APDS disease.

claim: Intervening PI3K/mTORC2 signaling can potentially result in harnessing NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses.
source: Our results suggest that intervening PI3K/mTORC2 signaling can potentially result in harnessing NAb induction against difficult-to-neutralize viruses.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings.

claim: NAb inducers showed persistent viremia with no significant difference in viral loads compared with NAb non-inducers.
source: These NAb inducers showed persistent viremia with no significant difference in viral loads compared with a subgroup of NAb non-inducers (n = 19) that were previously profile-clarified, naïve, and major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) haplotype-balanced (used for comparison hereafter) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the viral load data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Plasma SIVmac239-NAb titers showed an average maximum titer of 1:16, being induced at an average of 48 weeks post-infection.
source: Plasma SIVmac239-NAb titers measured by 10 TCID50 SIVmac239 virus-killing assay showed an average maximum titer of 1:16, being induced at an average of 48 weeks post-infection (p.i.) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Two of the nine NAb inducers showed detectable NAb responses by 24 weeks p.i., while the remaining seven induced NAbs after 30 weeks p.i.
source: Two of the nine NAb inducers showed detectable NAb responses by 24 weeks p.i., while the remaining seven induced NAbs after 30 weeks p.i.
evidence: This is a direct report of the temporal analysis of NAb induction.

claim: Anti-SIVmac239 neutralizing activity was confirmed in immunoglobulin G (IgG) purified from plasma of NAb inducers.
source: Anti-SIVmac239 neutralizing activity was confirmed in immunoglobulin G (IgG) purified from plasma of these NAb inducers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the IgG neutralization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SIV Env-binding IgGs developed from early infection in both NAb inducers and non-rapid-progressing NAb non-inducers.
source: SIV Env-binding IgGs developed from early infection in both NAb inducers and non-rapid-progressing NAb non-inducers, the latter differing from rapid progressors known to manifest serological failure (Hirsch et al., 2004; Nakane et al., 2013; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the Env-binding antibody data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Titers of Env-binding IgG were not higher but rather lower at year 1 p.i. in the NAb inducers.
source: Titers of Env-binding IgG were not higher but rather lower at year 1 p.i. in the NAb inducers (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative comparison shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and C.

claim: The pattern of lower Env-binding IgG titers in NAb inducers was consistent with other reports.
source: This was consistent with other reports (Havenar-Daughton et al., 2016) and differing with gross B-cell enhancement in Nef-deleted SIV infection with enhanced anti-SIV binding antibody titers accompanying marginal neutralization (Adnan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Havenar-Daughton et al., 2016 and Adnan et al., 2016.

claim: NAb inducers and non-inducers showed similar patterns of variations in viral env sequences, mainly in variable regions 1, 2 and 4 (V1, V2, and V4).
source: NAb inducers and non-inducers showed similar patterns of variations in viral env sequences (Burns et al., 1993), mainly in variable regions 1, 2 and 4 (V1, V2, and V4) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by the sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Selection of a viral genome mutation resulting in G (glycine)-to-E (glutamic acid) substitution at residue 63 of Nef (Nef-G63E) was found in seven of the nine NAb inducers.
source: Strikingly, we found selection of a viral genome mutation resulting in G (glycine)-to-E (glutamic acid) substitution at residue 63 of Nef (Nef-G63E) in seven of the nine NAb inducers (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a key finding from the viral sequence analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Two inducers that did not select Nef-G63E were the early inducers detected for NAb positivity before 24 weeks p.i.
source: Two inducers that did not select Nef-G63E were the early inducers detected for NAb positivity before 24 weeks p.i.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the temporal analysis of mutations and NAb induction.

claim: The 63rd residue of Nef lies in the unstructured N-terminus of Nef, flanked by two α-helices conserved in SIVmac/SIVsmm.
source: This 63rd residue lies in the unstructured N-terminus of Nef, flanked by two α-helices conserved in SIVmac/SIVsmm (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The region containing the 63rd residue of Nef is generally polymorphic among HIV-1/HIV-2/SIV, occasionally being deleted in laboratory and primary isolate HIV-1 strains.
source: This region is generally polymorphic among HIV-1/HIV-2/SIV, occasionally being deleted in laboratory and primary isolate HIV-1 strains (Geyer et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Geyer et al., 2001.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers.
source: This mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers, including one rapid progressor (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and selection was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Selection of Nef-G63E was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers.
source: This mutation was found only in 2 of the 19 NAb non-inducers, including one rapid progressor (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and selection was significantly enriched in the NAb inducers compared to the 19 non-inducers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Analysis of Nef-G63E mutation frequencies in plasma viruses showed that Nef-G63E selection preceded or at least paralleled NAb induction.
source: Analysis of Nef-G63E mutation frequencies in plasma viruses showed that Nef-G63E selection preceded or at least paralleled NAb induction (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the temporal analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The seven NAb inducers selecting Nef-G63E elicited CD8+ T-cell responses specific for a 9-mer peptide Nef62–70 QW9 (QGQYMNTPW).
source: We found that these seven NAb inducers selecting this mutation elicited CD8+ T-cell responses specific for a 9-mer peptide Nef62–70 QW9 (QGQYMNTPW) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the CD8+ T-cell response data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Nef62–70 QW9 epitope is restricted by MHC-I molecules Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01.
source: This Nef62–70 QW9 epitope is restricted by MHC-I molecules Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01 (Evans et al., 1999; Sette et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Evans et al., 1999 and Sette et al., 2012.

claim: Possession of Mamu-B*004:01 and Mamu-B*039:01 accounted for six cases of Nef-G63E selection.
source: Possession of these accounted for six cases of Nef-G63E selection (Figure 3A), and the remaining one animal possessed Mamu-A1*032:02 predicted to bind to Nef63–70 GW8 (NetMHCpan).
evidence: This is based on MHC-I genotyping and epitope prediction analysis.

claim: Nef-G63E was confirmed to be an escape mutation from Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses.
source: Nef-G63E was confirmed to be an escape mutation from Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by the T-cell response data to wild-type and mutant peptides shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NAb non-inducers possessing the relevant MHC-I alleles elicited little or no Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses.
source: NAb non-inducers possessing these alleles elicited little or no Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that in vivo selection and fixation of this Nef-G63E SIV was indeed Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T cell-dependent.
evidence: This is supported by the T-cell response data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line.
source: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line (Akari et al., 1996), excluding the possibility that the mutation critically impairs viral replication (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), and plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the viral replication data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers.
source: Replication of SIV carrying the Nef-G63E mutation was comparable with WT on a cynomolgus macaque HSC-F CD4+ T-cell line (Akari et al., 1996), excluding the possibility that the mutation critically impairs viral replication (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), and plasma viral loads were comparable between Nef-G63E mutant-selecting NAb inducers versus non-inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the viral load comparison shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Nef-G63E mutation did not confer notable change in downregulation of CD3, CD4, MHC-I, CXCR4, and BST-2 compared with WT.
source: Nef-G63E mutation did not confer notable change compared with WT (p=not significant [n.s.] for all molecules, data not shown), implicating other non-canonical changes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by the surface molecule downregulation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Plasma ferritin levels showed no differences between Nef-G63E-selecting NAb inducers and non-inducers.
source: Here, plasma ferritin levels showed no differences (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and viral loads were comparable as aforementioned between Nef-G63E-selecting NAb inducers and non-inducers, arguing against gross involvement of ferritin as well as other viral replication-related Nef phenotypes at least in this model.
evidence: This is supported by the ferritin measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The serine 473-phosphorylated form of Akt (pAkt Ser473) was significantly lower in Nef-G63E mutant-infected cells compared with WT.
source: This analysis revealed that its serine 473-phosphorylated form (pAkt Ser473), non-canonically known for Nef-mediated upregulation (Kumar et al., 2016), was significantly lower in Nef-G63E mutant-infected cells compared with WT (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the pAkt Ser473 measurement data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The difference in pAkt Ser473 levels was more pronounced than histogram deviation levels in PI3K gain-of-function mice with full recapitulation of B-cell/antibody-dysregulating human APDS disease phenotype.
source: The difference observed here was more pronounced than histogram deviation levels in PI3K gain-of-function mice with full recapitulation of B-cell/antibody-dysregulating human APDS disease phenotype (Avery et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current data and cited literature.

claim: The threonine 308-phosphorylated Akt (pAkt Thr308) level remained unaffected by Nef-G63E mutation.
source: In contrast, the threonine 308-phosphorylated Akt (pAkt Thr308) level remained unaffected (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the pAkt Thr308 measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: External PI3K stimuli by serum starvation accelerated phenotype appearance from day 3 to day 1 p.i.
source: Interestingly, external PI3K stimuli by serum starvation (Kennedy et al., 1997) accelerated phenotype appearance from day 3 to day 1 p.i. (Figure 4C, left).
evidence: This is supported by the serum starvation experiment data shown in Figure 4C, left.

claim: A high-MOI SIV infection accelerated phenotype appearance from day 3 to day 1 p.i., with stronger pAkt reduction.
source: A high-MOI SIV infection, comprising higher initial concentration of extracellular Env stimuli, also accelerated phenotype appearance from day 3 to day 1 p.i., with stronger pAkt reduction (Figure 4C, right).
evidence: This is supported by the high-MOI infection experiment data shown in Figure 4C, right.

claim: The Akt-inhibitory G63E mutant Nef phenotype is PI3K stimuli-dependent.
source: These data indicate that the Akt-inhibitory G63E mutant Nef phenotype is PI3K stimuli-dependent.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the serum starvation and high-MOI infection experiments.

claim: Transcriptome analysis signatured decrease in PI3K-pAkt-FoxO1-related genes in mutant SIV infection.
source: Transcriptome analysis signatured decrease in PI3K-pAkt-FoxO1-related genes in mutant SIV infection (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the transcriptome analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation causes significant decrease in Nef binding to PI3K p85/p110α and downstream mTORC2 components mTOR and GβL/mLST8.
source: We found that this Nef-G63E mutation causes significant decrease in Nef binding to PI3K p85/p110α and downstream mTORC2 components mTOR (Sarbassov et al., 2005) and GβL/mLST8 (Kim et al., 2003) in the CD4lo-SIV Gag p27+ infected population (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by the proximity ligation assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There was a decrease in G63E-mutated Nef binding to the mTORC2-intrinsic cofactor Sin1 in coimmunoprecipitation analysis.
source: Results were biochemically confirmed by a decrease in G63E-mutated Nef binding to the mTORC2-intrinsic cofactor Sin1 in coimmunoprecipitation analysis of infected HSC-F cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation attenuates PI3K/mTORC2 signaling driven by aberrant Nef bridging.
source: Collectively, the Nef-G63E mutation attenuates PI3K/mTORC2 signaling driven by aberrant Nef bridging, explaining decreased Akt Ser473 phosphorylation by mTORC2.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the collective experimental findings.

claim: Nef-G63E SIV infection resulted in more pronounced apoptosis of CD4-downregulated/infected HSC-F cells.
source: These properties were in keeping with more pronounced apoptosis of CD4-downregulated/infected HSC-F cells upon Nef-G63E SIV infection (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by the cell death assay data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Nef-G63E SIV is a mutant virus decreased in aberrant interaction/drive of B-cell-inhibitory PI3K/mTORC2 signaling, manifesting a molecular signature reciprocal to human APDS.
source: Thus, Nef-G63E SIV is a mutant virus decreased in aberrant interaction/drive of B-cell-inhibitory PI3K/mTORC2 signaling, manifesting a molecular signature reciprocal to human APDS (Angulo et al., 2013; Lucas et al., 2014; Avery et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the collective experimental findings and comparison with APDS.

claim: Lymph node Env-specific B cells showed significantly higher Nef-positive frequencies as compared with batch non-Env-specific B cells.
source: Strikingly, lymph node Env-specific B cells showed significantly higher Nef-positive frequencies as compared with batch non-Env-specific B cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by the imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Infected cell-derived Nef preferentially targets adjacent Env-specific B cells, putatively through its contact/transfer from infected CD4+ cells to B cells.
source: This indicated that infected cell-derived Nef preferentially targets adjacent Env-specific B cells, putatively through its contact/transfer from infected CD4+ cells to B cells (Xu et al., 2009; Hashimoto et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the imaging flow cytometry data and cited literature.

claim: The phenotypic change in Nef can directly dictate Env-specific B-cell maturation.
source: Thus, the phenotypic change in Nef can directly dictate Env-specific B-cell maturation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the preferential targeting of Env-specific B cells by Nef.

claim: Nef invasion upregulated pAkt Ser473 in Nef-invaded B cells in vivo to a range resembling in vitro analysis.
source: Nef invasion upregulated pAkt Ser473 (Ch 03) to a range resembling in vitro analysis (Figure 5C), demonstrating that Nef-driven aberrant PI3K/mTORC2 signaling does occur in Nef-invaded B cells in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by the pAkt Ser473 measurement in Nef+ B cells shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Addition of soluble, stimulation-competent antibodies against macaque CD3 enhanced adhesion of Nef+ T cells to B cells.
source: Importantly, addition of soluble, stimulation-competent antibodies against macaque CD3 enhanced adhesion of Nef+ T cells to B cells (Figure 6A, bottom center).
evidence: This is supported by the imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: An enhancement of live singlet Ramos B-cell Nef acquisition was observed by CD3 stimulation in conventional flow cytometry.
source: Substantiated by the acquired images, an enhancement of live singlet Ramos B-cell Nef acquisition (% Nef+ in total B cells) was also observed by CD3 stimulation in conventional flow cytometry (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by the flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In a 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells, there was recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef.
source: In a similar 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells, we detected recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef (Figure 6C), indicating that the Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.
evidence: This is supported by the coculture experiment data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.
source: In a similar 72-hour static coculture with primary CD20+ B cells, we detected recapitulation of the decreased B-cell pAkt Ser473 phosphorylation upon G63E Nef transfer compared to that of WT Nef (Figure 6C), indicating that the Nef-G63E mutation can directly alleviate maturation inhibition in preferentially Nef-targeted Env-specific B cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the coculture experiment data.

claim: NAb inducers showed significantly higher Env-specific IgG+ PB responses around week 30 p.i., after Nef-G63E selection, compared to those in NAb non-inducers.
source: NAb inducers showed significantly higher Env-specific IgG+ PB responses around week 30 p.i., after Nef-G63E selection, compared to those in NAb non-inducers (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the plasmablast frequency data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: At 1 year, the difference in Env-specific PB frequencies became enhanced as a result of less pronounced decrease in Env-specific PB frequencies in the NAb inducers.
source: At 1 year, this difference became enhanced as a result of less pronounced decrease in Env-specific PB frequencies in the NAb inducers.
evidence: This is based on the temporal analysis of plasmablast frequencies shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: In NAb non-inducers, all vectors converged on an empirically defined polygonal attractor area Dn at year 1 p.i. and beyond.
source: In NAb non-inducers, all vectors converged on an empirically defined polygonal attractor area Dn (gray area surrounded with dotted lines in Figure 7D, right) at year 1 p.i. and beyond, describing that these NAb non-inducers failed to sustain Env-specific GC output.
evidence: This is based on the two-dimensional vector analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The vectors were consistently tracked outside Dn in the NAb inducers with Nef-G63E.
source: In contrast, the vectors were consistently tracked outside Dn in the NAb inducers with Nef-G63E (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is based on the two-dimensional vector analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: At the time of NAb induction, NAb inducer vectors converged on another upper-right GC output attractor area Di that is mutually exclusive with Dn.
source: At the time of NAb induction, they converged on another upper-right GC output attractor area Di (red area surrounded with dotted lines in Figure 7D, right) that is mutually exclusive with Dn (p<0.0001 by Fisher's exact test on NAb non-inducer/inducer vector distribution frequency within Dn).
evidence: This is based on the two-dimensional vector analysis and statistical testing shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The findings suggest more robust virus-specific IgG+ B-cell responses following Nef-G63E CD8+ T-cell escape mutant selection, ultimately leading to NAb induction.
source: These suggest more robust virus-specific IgG+ B-cell responses following Nef-G63E CD8+ T-cell escape mutant selection, ultimately leading to NAb induction.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the B-cell response data.

claim: The enhanced signature of cognate B cells was also an inverted pattern of impaired terminal differentiation of B-cell responses in APDS.
source: The enhanced signature of cognate B cells was also an inverted pattern of impaired terminal differentiation of B-cell responses in APDS (Al Qureshah et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current findings and cited literature on APDS.

claim: In the current model, Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses in persistently SIVmac239-infected macaques selected for an escape mutant, Nef-G63E, which displays attenuated aberrant Nef binding and ensuing drive of B-cell-inhibitory PI3K/mTORC2.
source: Taken together, in the current model, Nef62-70-specific CD8+ T-cell responses in persistently SIVmac239-infected macaques selected for an escape mutant, Nef-G63E, which displays attenuated aberrant Nef binding and ensuing drive of B-cell-inhibitory PI3K/mTORC2.
evidence: This is a summary of the key findings from the study.

claim: Nef invasion of B cells in vivo occurred more preferentially in Env-specific B cells, suggesting diminution in Nef-mediated tonic dysregulation of B cells after mutant selection.
source: Nef invasion of B cells in vivo occurred more preferentially in Env-specific B cells, suggesting diminution in Nef-mediated tonic dysregulation of B cells after mutant selection.
evidence: This is based on the imaging flow cytometry data showing preferential Nef targeting of Env-specific B cells.

claim: These events conceivably predisposed to enhanced Env-specific B-cell responses and subsequent SIVmac239-specific NAb induction, altogether, in a manner reciprocal to human APDS-mediated immune dysregulation.
source: These events conceivably predisposed to enhanced Env-specific B-cell responses and subsequent SIVmac239-specific NAb induction, altogether, in a manner reciprocal to human APDS-mediated immune dysregulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the collective findings and comparison with APDS.

claim: The current Nef-G63E-associated B-cell/NAb phenotype likely occurs in a 'reciprocal APDS-like' manner.
source: Thus, the current Nef-G63E-associated B-cell/NAb phenotype likely occurs in a 'reciprocal APDS-like' manner.
evidence: This is an interpretive conclusion based on the comparison with APDS disease.

claim: This work is the first to interlink a PI3K/mTORC2-modulating viral signature and enhanced B-cell/NAb responses in a viral infection model.
source: This work is, to our knowledge, the first to interlink a PI3K/mTORC2-modulating viral signature and enhanced B-cell/NAb responses in a viral infection model.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Enhanced binding of mutant HIV-1 epitope peptide to inhibitory MHC-I on DCs impairs T cells.
source: For example, enhanced binding of mutant HIV-1 epitope peptide to inhibitory MHC-I on DCs impairs T cells (Lichterfeld et al., 2007) and decreased CTL-mediated lymph node immunopathology can drive, and not inhibit, the production of LCMV-specific antibodies (Battegay et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lichterfeld et al., 2007.

claim: Decreased CTL-mediated lymph node immunopathology can drive, and not inhibit, the production of LCMV-specific antibodies.
source: For example, enhanced binding of mutant HIV-1 epitope peptide to inhibitory MHC-I on DCs impairs T cells (Lichterfeld et al., 2007) and decreased CTL-mediated lymph node immunopathology can drive, and not inhibit, the production of LCMV-specific antibodies (Battegay et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Battegay et al., 1993.

claim: The results evidence a new pattern of NAb responses that are bivalently shaped through viral interactions with both humoral and cellular immunity in AIDS virus infection.
source: Our results now evidence a new pattern of NAb responses that are bivalently shaped through viral interactions with both humoral and cellular immunity in AIDS virus infection.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the significance of the findings.

claim: SIVmac239 infection of macaques possessing MHC-I alleles associated with Nef-G63E mutation can be one unique platform to analyze virus–host interaction for B cell maturation leading to NAb induction.
source: SIVmac239 infection of macaques possessing MHC-I alleles associated with Nef-G63E mutation can be one unique platform to analyze virus–host interaction for B cell maturation leading to NAb induction.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the utility of the model system.

claim: The interval between Nef-G63E mutant selection and NAb induction was variable in the NAb inducers.
source: The interval between Nef-G63E mutant selection and NAb induction was variable in the NAb inducers, for which we did not obtain a clear explanation.
evidence: This is an observation from the temporal analysis.

claim: The variability in interval between Nef-G63E mutant selection and NAb induction may be influenced by certain basal competitive balance between humoral versus cellular adaptive immunity.
source: This may be influenced by certain basal competitive balance between humoral versus cellular adaptive immunity (Recher et al., 2007), as observed in certain vaccination settings (Querec et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by citations.

claim: The current Nef-G63E phenotype adds yet another aspect to the wealth of evidence documenting the multifaceted impact of Nef in HIV/SIV infection.
source: The current Nef-G63E phenotype identified here adds yet another aspect to the wealth of evidence documenting the multifaceted impact of Nef in HIV/SIV infection (Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Gauduin et al., 2006; Stolp et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a contextual statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: The current phenotype differed from decreased replication-related properties or generalized amelioration in immune impairment such as those of delta-Nef HIV/SIV.
source: Based on our data, the current phenotype differed from decreased replication-related properties or generalized amelioration in immune impairment such as those of delta-Nef HIV/SIV (Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Johnson et al., 1997; Gauduin et al., 2006; Fukazawa et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current findings and cited literature.

claim: The SIV Nef N-terminal unstructured region comprising Nef-G63E is not conserved in HIV-1.
source: The SIV Nef N-terminal unstructured region comprising Nef-G63E is not conserved in HIV-1 (Schindler et al., 2004), and beyond this model study it remains to be addressed whether a mutant HIV-1 with a similar immunosignaling-related phenotype can be obtained and how much lentiviral conservation exists for such interactions.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schindler et al., 2004.

claim: Preferential Nef transfer to Env-specific B cells suggests potential involvement of polarized perturbation in cognate immune cells in vivo.
source: Preferential Nef transfer to Env-specific B cells (Figure 5) suggests potential involvement of polarized perturbation in cognate immune cells in vivo, which was best depicted for preferential infectivity of HIV-specific CD4+ T cells (Douek et al., 2002) and HIV condensation to the interface of DC-T-cell contacts (McDonald et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on the imaging flow cytometry data and cited literature.

claim: Cognate MHC class II interactions regularly occur between HIV/SIV-specific CD4+ T cells and Env-specific B cells in GCs.
source: As cognate MHC class II interactions (Wülfing et al., 1998; Gitlin et al., 2014) regularly occur between HIV/SIV-specific CD4+ T cells and Env-specific B cells in GCs, dysregulation of Env-specific B cells may well result from hijacking of cognate T-cell/B-cell interactions by the virus.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wülfing et al., 1998 and Gitlin et al., 2014.

claim: Enhanced T-cell attachment and transfer of Nef to B cells by TCR stimulation may override constraints of infection-mediated CD4+ T-cell cytoskeletal impairment.
source: Enhanced T-cell attachment and transfer of Nef to B cells by TCR stimulation (Figure 6) may override constraints of infection-mediated CD4+ T-cell cytoskeletal impairment (Campbell et al., 2004; Jolly et al., 2004; Stolp et al., 2009), particularly by antagonizing reduced motility (Stolp et al., 2012), resulting in in vivo 'filtering' of enhanced cognate CD4+ T-cell interaction with cognate B cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the coculture experiment data and cited literature.

claim: Tfh cells that bear trogocytosed CD20 and are positive for viral DNA appear in vivo during SIV infection and increase when infection progresses.
source: Interestingly, Tfh cells that bear trogocytosed CD20 and are positive for viral DNA appear in vivo during SIV infection and increase when infection progresses (Samer et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Samer et al., 2023.

claim: The major in vivo readout of this study is autologous neutralization of a highly difficult-to-neutralize SIV strain, which is different from HIV-specific broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs).
source: The major in vivo readout of this study is autologous neutralization of a highly difficult-to-neutralize SIV strain, which is different from HIV-specific broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs).
evidence: This is a clarification about the nature of the NAb responses studied.

claim: Obtained signatures of enhanced IgG+ Env-specific AFC and B cells (class switch/terminal differentiation) and virus neutralization (hypermutation) are indicative of elevated activity of activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID).
source: Importantly, however, obtained signatures of enhanced IgG+ Env-specific AFC and B cells (class switch/terminal differentiation) and virus neutralization (hypermutation) in our model are indicative of elevated activity of activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), the canonical positive driver of B-cell fate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the B-cell response data and knowledge of AID function.

claim: Findings in this study have a strong conceptual continuity with bNAb regulation by AID in HIV infection.
source: Thus, we reason that findings in this study have a strong conceptual continuity with bNAb regulation by AID in HIV infection.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement about the broader significance of the findings.

claim: The results extracted an in vivo link between a decrease in aberrant Nef-PI3K/mTORC2 interaction and major enhancement in B-cell responses.
source: Our results extracted an in vivo link between a decrease in aberrant Nef-PI3K/mTORC2 interaction and major enhancement in B-cell responses.
evidence: This is a summary of the key finding from the study.

claim: The relationship between decreased Nef-PI3K/mTORC2 interaction and enhanced B-cell responses is reciprocal to immunogenetic mechanisms of human PI3K gain-of-function mutations, resulting in APDS with multiply impaired antiviral B-cell responses.
source: The relationship is reciprocal to immunogenetic mechanisms of human PI3K gain-of-function mutations, resulting in APDS with multiply impaired antiviral B-cell responses.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the relationship between the findings and APDS.

claim: APDS occurs from germline mutations in leukocyte-intrinsic p110δ catalytic subunit-coding PIK3CD or the ubiquitous p85α regulatory subunit-coding PIK3R1.
source: APDS occurs from germline mutations in leukocyte-intrinsic p110δ catalytic subunit-coding PIK3CD or the ubiquitous p85α regulatory subunit-coding PIK3R1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about APDS.

claim: In APDS, the mutations cause residue substitutions, resulting in class IA PI3K gain of function.
source: In both cases, the mutations cause residue substitutions, resulting in class IA PI3K gain of function (Dornan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dornan et al., 2017.

claim: Hyperactivated PI3K interferes with cognate B cells in an immune cell-intrinsic manner, leading to impaired B-cell class switching and resultant susceptibility against various infections.
source: Hyperactivated PI3K interferes with cognate B cells in an immune cell-intrinsic manner, leading to impaired B-cell class switching and resultant susceptibility against various infections (Angulo et al., 2013; Lucas et al., 2014; Coulter et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Angulo et al., 2013; Lucas et al., 2014; and Coulter et al., 2017.

claim: The current work documents a decrease in virally induced tonic PI3K drive, enhanced IgG class-switched cognate B-cell responses and NAb induction against a notably difficult-to-neutralize SIV.
source: In the current work, we conversely document a decrease in virally induced tonic PI3K drive, enhanced IgG class-switched cognate B-cell responses and NAb induction against a notably difficult-to-neutralize SIV.
evidence: This is a summary of the key findings from the study.

claim: PI3Kp85 showed the strongest Nef-binding index in PLA assay presumably because of the SH3-binding PxxP domain in Nef, which binds the SH3 domain of PI3Kp85.
source: Yet PI3Kp85 showed the strongest Nef-binding index in PLA assay (Figure 4D) presumably because of the SH3-binding PxxP domain in Nef, which binds the SH3 domain of PI3Kp85 (Rickles et al., 1994).
evidence: This is based on the PLA data and cited literature on Nef-PI3K interactions.

claim: Decreased binding of Nef to its canonical target PI3Kp85 may precipitate into attenuated interactions of Nef with quintuple PI3K/mTORC2, resulting in fragile downstream Akt signaling.
source: Decreased binding of Nef to its canonical target PI3Kp85 may precipitate into attenuated interactions of Nef with quintuple PI3K/mTORC2, resulting in fragile downstream Akt signaling.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the binding data.

claim: Such domino-triggering is also observed in APDS patients, from gain-of-function mutant p85 to p110.
source: Such domino-triggering is also observed in APDS patients, from gain-of-function mutant p85 to p110 (Dornan et al., 2017), which similarly illustrates the fine-tuned nature of the PI3K/mTORC2/Akt signaling pathway.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dornan et al., 2017.

claim: A limitation of this study is the use of retrospective samples, posing constraints for detecting exact temporal changes in tonic viral B-cell perturbation.
source: A limitation of this study is the use of retrospective samples, posing constraints for detecting exact temporal changes in tonic viral B-cell perturbation.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a study limitation.

claim: HIV/SIV infection uniquely shows a biphasic Tfh dysregulation of acute-phase destruction followed by dysregulated chronic-phase hyper-expansion.
source: HIV/SIV infection uniquely shows a biphasic Tfh dysregulation of acute-phase destruction Mattapallil et al., 2005; Moukambi et al., 2015; Moukambi et al., 2019 followed by dysregulated chronic-phase hyper-expansion (Lindqvist et al., 2012; Petrovas et al., 2012; Cubas et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations in PI3K-encoding genes appear to affect B cells more strongly.
source: Gain-of-function mutations in PI3K-encoding genes appear to affect B cells more strongly (Asano et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Asano et al., 2018.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations in PI3K-encoding genes also evoke basal dysregulation in peripheral CD4+ T cells, which locally recapitulates dysregulation and death of HIV/SIV-infected CD4+ T cells.
source: Nonetheless, it is noteworthy that they also evoke basal dysregulation in peripheral CD4+ T cells, which locally recapitulates dysregulation and death of HIV/SIV-infected CD4+ T cells, highlighting the importance of PI3K-mediated signaling in HIV/SIV infection.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between APDS and HIV/SIV infection.

claim: Specific animal models like the current one help to depict a temporal cascade of in vivo events leading to NAb induction, assisting human immunology.
source: In any event, we surmise that specific animal models like the current one help to depict a temporal cascade of in vivo events leading to NAb induction, assisting human immunology.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the utility of the model system.

claim: NAb induction against a difficult-to-neutralize SIV strain occurs after selection of a CD8+ T-cell escape variant with a reduced ability to drive excess PI3K/mTORC2 signaling.
source: In conclusion, we demonstrated in a non-human primate AIDS model that NAb induction against a difficult-to-neutralize SIV strain occurs after selection of a CD8+ T-cell escape variant with a reduced ability to drive excess PI3K/mTORC2 signaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: These results collectively offer an example of how NAb responses against immunodeficiency viruses can be shaped by both wings of adaptive immune pressure.
source: These results collectively offer an example of how NAb responses against immunodeficiency viruses can be shaped by both wings of adaptive immune pressure.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the significance of the findings.

claim: Given the key role for Nef-mediated perturbation of PI3K/mTORC2 in NAb resistance, immune cell-intrinsic PI3K/mTORC2 manipulation may offer a new possibility to harness antiviral NAb responses.
source: Given the key role for Nef-mediated perturbation of PI3K/mTORC2 in NAb resistance, immune cell-intrinsic PI3K/mTORC2 manipulation may offer a new possibility to harness antiviral NAb responses.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: As human IEIs are increasingly becoming discovered with various immune-perturbing phenotypes and inheritance patterns, search of other types of analogies between viral immune dysregulations and human IEIs may fuel the discovery of novel targets to modulate and harness immune responses in translational settings.
source: As human IEIs are increasingly becoming discovered with various immune-perturbing phenotypes and inheritance patterns (Jauch et al., 2023), search of other types of analogies between viral immune dysregulations and human IEIs may fuel the discovery of novel targets to modulate and harness immune responses in translational settings.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.
